images.caption:
A large Coccinellid beetle, commonly called Harlequin ladybird, has been submitted to the NTNU University Museum in Trondheim. This is the first sighting of this unwelcome species in Trondheim. 
The Harlequin ladybird (Harmonia Axyridis) was found on a porch in Tiller, south of Trondheim. The house-owner, Alf Ivar Oterholm, managed to catch the beetle and submitted it to the museum the 10th of June 2009.

images.filename: Reichskomissar-skilt funnet av marinarkeolog David Tuddenham.jpg
images.caption: On the 7th of December, 2009, a sign was recovered from Nidelva, Trondheim. It read ”Reichskommissar für die besetzten Norwegischen Gebiete Dienstelle Trondheim", which translates to "Reich Commissariat for the Norwegian occupied areas, Trondheim service area". The sign was discovered by  team of marine archeologists at NTNU University Museum; led by David Tuddenham, lead diver Trond Aurmo, and rescue diver Rasmus Svennson. The sign was most likely hung at Stiftsgården, at the office of Trondheim's Reich Commissariat.
